name: sweetalert2
description: A beautiful, responsive, customizable and accessible (WAI-ARIA) replacement for JavaScript's popup boxes, supported fork of sweetalert

readme.summary: The README provides a minimal description and links to external docs, but contains almost no actual documentation — just sponsor tables (including NSFW content) with no inline installation, usage examples, or configuration.
readme.top_issue: The README is essentially empty of technical content, deferring everything to external links with no inline quick-start, code examples, or installation instructions.

common_complaints: iOS Safari scrolling issues with long modals and backdrop:false
Z-index/layering problems with dialogs and Material Design overlays
CSS bleeding from host pages into dialogs
Content Security Policy (CSP) compatibility with nonce-based styles
Focus management issues in form validation workflows
praise_themes: Respectful, well-documented issue reports from users
Relatively quick closure of reported issues
sentiment.summary: SweetAlert2 is actively maintained with timely fixes, but has persistent platform-specific issues (particularly iOS) and styling isolation concerns that suggest resource constraints or lower priority architectural problems.

concerns: Zero commits in the past 6 months despite 6 open issues
No merged PRs in the past 6 months
Unresolved open issues without recent attention
Zero closed issues in the past 6 months
Last release date unknown - cannot verify currency of available version
positive_signals: No open PRs pending review (clear backlog)
maintenance.summary: sweetalert2 appears abandoned with no development activity, contributor engagement, or issue resolution over the past 6 months despite 6 unresolved issues.
